source_scope.source_detail_limit: The prototype combines legal identity, onboarding workflow, mutable merchant profile, payout, deposit, appeal and AI interaction data. It contains raw identity documents, bank/card data, addresses and free-form content, and the exit heading creates the withdraw table. Every authority and restricted field therefore requires an explicit split.

verification_policy.specified_definition: A merchant source is specified only when a same-name detailed DDL proves the asset and its tenant, legal identity, money, workflow, security, history, authority, corrections and runtime gate are explicit.
verification_policy.verified_definition: Verification requires a non-empty production evidence bundle and full-denominator tenant-scoped independent zero-difference reconciliation.

lifecycle_policy_defaults.history_policy: Append onboarding, legal-entity, merchant, agreement, payout, deposit, appeal and AI interaction facts independently; mutable daily snapshots are observations, never history authority.
lifecycle_policy_defaults.delete_policy: Source deletion retires current visibility but never erases legal approvals, money ledger entries, appeals, payout attempts, deposit evidence or audit lineage.
lifecycle_policy_defaults.backfill_policy: Resolve tenant, Principal, Merchant, LegalEntity, Shop, bank token, payment, SPU and source mappings before replay; quarantine unknown statuses, ambiguous units, raw secrets, orphan effects and cross-aggregate identity guesses.

assets.source_grain: one mutable merchant-onboarding application snapshot per source id

semantic_rules.grain: one onboarding case references a separately versioned legal entity, Merchant candidate, operators and deposit requirement
semantic_rules.identity: user, merchant, legal entity, corporation, contact and approver identities are distinct tenant-scoped references
semantic_rules.money_or_quantity: initial deposit is int64 minor units plus ISO currency; settlement cadence and fee policy are separate versioned contracts
semantic_rules.history: every review/legal/agreement/deposit transition appends; status 800 is not evidence of Shop creation
semantic_rules.security: license, ID cards, phones, addresses and approver lists are tokenized or restricted encrypted evidence and forbidden from events
semantic_rules.authority: Merchant owns onboarding and Merchant lifecycle; Identity owns Principals; LegalEntity owns regulated identity; no Shop may be invented from merchant_id

corrections: split legal identity, onboarding, merchant and deposit requirement
replace acl_ids and names with versioned Principal assignments
do not create a Shop without an exact Shop source or approved command

assets.source_grain: one mutable daily merchant information snapshot per merchant_id

semantic_rules.grain: one observed profile must split into independently versioned Merchant, legal, agreement, settlement, deposit and restricted address/payment references
semantic_rules.identity: merchant_id is a qualified source mapping; user, legal entity, bank account, contacts and addresses remain separate identities
semantic_rules.money_or_quantity: deposit and fee bounds require currency, minor units and rounding; string deposit_freeze/poundage_discount are quarantined until typed
semantic_rules.history: daily snapshots produce explicit changes and SCD history; later PII cannot rewrite facts accepted under an earlier agreement
semantic_rules.security: ID cards, bank account, phones, names and full addresses are tokenized/restricted and never emitted in canonical events
semantic_rules.authority: Merchant owns lifecycle/profile; LegalEntity owns regulated identity; Payment owns bank token; Deposit ledger owns money; Fulfillment owns address use

corrections: split overloaded mutable snapshot into independent authorities
tokenize bank and identity data before ingestion
reject deposit_freeze or fee discounts without typed amount/rate semantics

assets.source_grain: one mutable merchant appeal snapshot per source id

semantic_rules.grain: one appeal case with immutable submissions, evidence versions and decisions
semantic_rules.identity: appeal, Merchant, SPU, payout, deposit, supply-chain or penalty references depend on apply_type and remain distinct
semantic_rules.money_or_quantity: any granted money effect is a separate compensation/deposit/payout command, never encoded in appeal status

semantic_rules.security: reason and images remain restricted evidence with malware scan and access audit
semantic_rules.authority: Customer Service owns appeal workflow; the affected domain owns accepted effects

corrections: route apply_type through a versioned target dictionary
separate case decision from Merchant state
retain images as restricted references rather than raw event payload

assets.source_grain: one mutable merchant payout/withdrawal observation per order_no

semantic_rules.grain: one payout intent may have multiple immutable provider attempts and one posted merchant ledger effect
semantic_rules.identity: withdraw order, channel transaction, Merchant, user and bank token are separate tenant-scoped identities
semantic_rules.money_or_quantity: amount is int64 minor units but currency is absent, so every row is blocked until account currency is proven
semantic_rules.history: provider observations and payout transitions append; success/failure never overwrite attempts
semantic_rules.security: card_id is tokenized and raw PAN/account data is forbidden; reason and provider data are restricted
semantic_rules.authority: Payout owns withdrawal workflow; Ledger owns balance effect; Payment/bank vault owns instrument token; Merchant is reference only

corrections: add immutable payout attempts
prove currency from the exact account contract
never store or emit raw card_id

assets.source_grain: purported merchant-offboarding application per exit_no, unproven because the detailed DDL recreates the withdraw table

semantic_rules.grain: one versioned offboarding case coordinates penalties, listings, deposits, payout and final Merchant retirement
semantic_rules.identity: exit case, Merchant, requester Principal, penalty, unpublish saga and settlement ids remain distinct
semantic_rules.money_or_quantity: final deposit/payout/fee balances reconcile through their ledgers before retirement
semantic_rules.history: request, review, rejection and completion append and source deletion never erases the case
semantic_rules.security: mobile, merchant name and free-form reason remain restricted
semantic_rules.authority: Merchant owns offboarding orchestration; Listing, Deposit, Payout and penalty domains own their effects

corrections: do not execute the mislabeled withdraw DDL as an exit source
require a physical exit schema before specification
coordinate offboarding through durable cross-domain checkpoints

assets.source_grain: one merchant deposit recharge application/provider observation per recharge_no

semantic_rules.grain: one immutable deposit ledger posting references one separately observed payment/provider transaction
semantic_rules.identity: recharge, provider transaction, Merchant, user Principal and ledger entry ids remain distinct
semantic_rules.money_or_quantity: amount is STRING and generic-unit, so parse only through currency-specific decimal/unit/rounding evidence into int64 minor units
semantic_rules.history: application, payment observation, approval and ledger posting append with idempotency
semantic_rules.security: voucher and remark are restricted; public events expose only digest/reference
semantic_rules.authority: Merchant Deposit ledger owns held funds; Payment owns money movement; Merchant lifecycle only consumes deposit readiness

corrections: convert generic string amount only with exact currency/unit proof
separate provider transaction from deposit ledger posting
store voucher as restricted evidence

assets.source_grain: one merchant assistant question-answer interaction per source id

semantic_rules.grain: one invocation attempt plus independent adoption/like/dislike feedback observations
semantic_rules.identity: interaction, invocation, Merchant, model/workflow version, data access and feedback ids remain distinct
semantic_rules.money_or_quantity: money in natural-language answers is not a financial fact; structured metrics require source metric/unit lineage
semantic_rules.history: prompt, response, model/data versions and each feedback transition append without rewriting
semantic_rules.security: question, answer, suggested questions, merchant name and table list are restricted and may contain PII, secrets or operational schema
semantic_rules.authority: AI Operations owns invocation/feedback; Merchant is context; business domains and Metadata own facts and lineage

corrections: store prompt/response as restricted references rather than event payload
bind exact model/workflow and governed dataset versions
do not treat generated answers as Order, Refund or finance authority
